Alabama.intent: 1 coming off a down screen from 5 at the elbow for a layup or a pull-up in the lane, with 4 relocating to the wing as the secondary option
Alabama.advantage: We create it by forcing the defense to rotate through multiple cuts and ball reversals, then hitting 1's defender with a down screen when they're ball-watching. The constant weak-side movement occupies help defenders so they can't tag the screen.
Alabama.entry: 1 dribbles left to the wing, which triggers 2 to cut up to the top. This gets the defense in rotation from the start and empties the right side for the finish.

beatPurposes.b1: Initial alignment and spacing — get 1 to the wing and clear the right side by bringing 2 up top
beatPurposes.b2: Ball reversal to the elbow — this shifts the defense and sets up the screening angle while 3's cut occupies weak-side help
beatPurposes.b3: Decision beat — 5 reads what the defense gives with multiple options, keeps them rotating and prevents them from loading up on the screen
beatPurposes.b4: Payoff — down screen for 1 cutting to the rim, with 4 relocating as the kick option if help comes

progression: First look: Attack the rim — you should have separation and the help is occupied

Third look: Kick to 4 on the wing if help rotates from the right side
reads.trigger: Read your defender. If he goes under, pull it. If he trails, you have the rim. If the tag comes hard from 2's man, 4 is open on the wing.

reads.situation: You just received the pass on the left wing

1.job: You're the primary scorer. Start the play with the dribble to the wing, relocate to the right side, then come hard off 5's screen looking for your shot at the rim or in the lane.
keys: Set up your cut — don't drift toward the screen early or your defender will beat you over it
Read the screen — if your man goes under, pull up; if he trails, attack the rim
Come off it at game speed — this isn't a jog, you're trying to score
1.commonError: Floating toward the screen too early instead of holding your spot, which lets your defender cheat over the top and kill the action

2.job: You start in the right corner, then cut to the top of the key to clear space and occupy your defender. After that, hold the right slot to provide a pressure release and keep the floor spaced.
keys: Your cut in beat 1 clears the right side — don't be late or you'll clog 1's finishing space
Stay above the break after you relocate — if you drift down, you shrink the spacing for 1's cut
Be ready as an outlet if the play breaks down
2.commonError: Drifting back toward the wing after cutting up, which brings your defender into the driving lane and kills 1's angle to the rim

3.job: You're in the left corner. When the ball goes to 5, you cut along the three-point line to the wing, then make the pass to 5 at the elbow to trigger the down screen. Your movement occupies weak-side help.
keys: Your cut in beat 2 keeps your defender honest — don't just stand and watch
Hit 5 quickly when you catch it on the wing — the timing of this pass triggers the screen
After you pass, stay wide and be ready for a skip if the defense collapses
3.commonError: Standing still in the corner instead of cutting, which lets your defender sink in and become the tag defender on 1's cut

4.job: You start at the right elbow, then relocate to the top as a passing option for 5. Finally, you cut to the right wing to be the kick option when 1 comes off the screen.
keys: Don't leave the top too early in beat 3 — 5 might need you as a pressure release
Time your cut to the wing with 1's screen — you're the safety valve if help rotates
Be shot-ready when you catch it on the wing — this should be a clean catch-and-shoot
4.commonError: Cutting to the wing too early, before 5 makes a decision, which eliminates you as a top-of-key option and makes the play predictable

5.job: You're the facilitator. Start at the left elbow, receive the pass from 1, read the defense with multiple options in beat 3, then set a solid down screen for 1 at the right elbow.
keys: Read the defense in beat 3 — if they collapse, you have options; if they stay home, you're screening next
Set the screen at the elbow level — not too high or 1 has no driving angle, not too low or there's no separation
After you screen, slip to the basket if your man helps hard on 1
5.commonError: Setting the screen too high or at the wrong angle, which forces 1 away from the rim instead of creating a straight-line drive to the basket

Make contact on the screen, then read your defender — if he shows, slip; if he stays home, roll weak side
Your cut to the basket in beat 1 occupies your defender early so he can't help on the initial action

progression: Curl to the wing for the catch-and-shoot three if your man trails
Fade if your man cheats under and takes away the curl
Reject the screen and cut backdoor if your man top-locks you
reads.trigger: Read your defender's position as you approach the screen—trailing means curl, under means fade, denial means reject

1.job: You start with the ball at the top. Dribble over and hit 4 on the wing to initiate, then relocate weak side to keep your defender honest and provide a safety outlet
keys: Move the ball quickly to get into the set—don't let the defense get set
After you pass, relocate to the weak wing or slot so you're available if the defense rotates
1.commonError: Standing still after the pass instead of relocating—your defender will then help on the main action

2.job: You cut to the right corner initially, then move up to receive the ball and deliver the pass to 4 coming off the screen. You're the trigger man
keys: Time your movement from corner to slot so you're ready to catch when 4 is coming off the screen
Make the pass on time and on target—4 needs it in his shooting pocket
2.commonError: Being late getting from the corner to the slot, which delays the whole action and lets the defense recover

3.job: You cut to the left corner and stay there. Your job is to occupy your defender and keep the weak-side help from rotating to help on 4
keys: Get to the corner early and stay there—don't drift up
Be a threat—hands ready, show you're an option if the ball swings
3.commonError: Drifting up toward the wing or watching the play—if you come up, your defender helps on the screen and kills the shot

4.job: You start on the left wing, then relocate to set up the screen. Come hard off 5's down screen to the right wing for the catch-and-shoot three
keys: Set your man up—walk him down before you use the screen so you get separation
Come off the screen ready to shoot—hands up, on balance, no wasted motion
4.commonError: Coming off the screen too early before it's set, or not being ready to shoot immediately on the catch

5.job: You stay at the high post initially to keep your defender from helping, then set a solid down screen for 4. After the screen, read whether to slip, pop, or roll based on how your defender plays it
keys: Stay high until the action starts—if you drop early, your man helps weak-side
Set the screen at the proper angle and depth—elbow area, giving 4 room to come to the wing
After contact, read your defender and either slip to the rim or pop out if he helps hard on 4
5.commonError: Setting the screen too high or too shallow—4 needs space to come to the wing for the three, not jammed into the sideline

spacingRules: 3 stays in the left corner until the ball moves—no drifting up or you bring your defender into the help
1 must relocate after the initial pass—standing still allows your defender to help on the main screen
5 stays at the high post initially—if you drop too early, your defender can help weak-side and then recover to the screen

counters.trigger: 4's defender goes under the screen and takes away the curl to the wing
counters.response: 4 fades behind the screen for the three instead of curling—5 can adjust the angle to help create this
counters.why: If the defender goes under, he's taking away the curl but giving up the fade—you get the same shot, different spot

counters.trigger: 5's defender hedges hard or shows on 4 coming off the screen
counters.response: 5 slips to the rim or pops back out—2 hits 5 instead of 4
counters.why: If 5's man helps on 4, he can't guard 5—someone's open, and it's often 5 with a better look than 4 had

counters.trigger: 4's defender top-locks or denies hard before the screen
counters.response: 4 rejects the screen and cuts backdoor to the rim—2 delivers the pass for the layup
counters.why: Overplay always gives up the back cut—if he's denying the catch, the basket is wide open

counters.trigger: The defense switches the screen
counters.response: 4 takes the mismatch and either shoots over the smaller defender or 5 seals the smaller defender and posts up
counters.why: Switching creates a mismatch one way or the other—take advantage of whoever has the size or speed advantage

situations: Need a three-point look
When you have a shooter at the 4 who can move without the ball
Against teams that don't switch or hedge hard on down screens
After a timeout when you need a clean look
To get your 4 going early in the game with a quality touch

4 doesn't set up the screen properly—just runs at it without walking his defender down, so there's no separation
5 sets the screen too high or at the wrong angle—4 gets jammed into the sideline with no room for the shot
2 is late rotating from the corner to the slot—the timing is off and 4's defender recovers
1 doesn't relocate after the pass—stands and watches, so 1's defender helps on the screen

Horns.intent: 4 coming off a back screen from 5 for a layup at the rim, with 2 on the wing as the kick-out if help rotates
Horns.advantage: We force the defense to make multiple rotations—first on the cuts to reposition, then on the ball reversal, then on the back screen—so help is late or out of position when 4 cuts to the basket
Horns.entry: Horns alignment—1 at the top with the ball, 5 and 4 at the elbows, 2 and 3 in the corners. We initiate with 1 passing to 5 on the left elbow

beatPurposes.b1: Shift the defense with the pass to the elbow and use simultaneous cuts by 5, 4, and 2 to scramble help assignments and create confusion
beatPurposes.b2: Swing the ball quickly from 5 to 4 to 1 on the right side while 2 cuts through—this reversal forces the defense to rotate and sets up the back screen with their help out of position
beatPurposes.b3: Deliver the primary action—5 back screens for 4 cutting to the rim while 1 hits 2 on the wing, creating a two-way threat of the dive or the kick

reads.situation: You've received the ball on the right wing after the swing, and 5 is setting the back screen for 4
progression: First look: 2 cutting to the wing for the catch-and-shoot if your defender helps on 4's cut
Second look: 4 diving to the rim off the back screen if the defense doesn't rotate
Third look: 5 slipping to the basket if his defender shows hard on 4
reads.trigger: Read your defender—if he steps in to tag 4, hit 2 immediately. If he stays home, look at 4's defender—if he trails the screen, hit 4 on the dive. If 5's man jumps the screen early, 5 slips and you hit him

reads.situation: You're about to receive the back screen from 5
progression: First look: Cut hard off the screen to the rim with your hands up
Second look: If the defense switches or hedges hard, short roll to the middle for the pocket pass
reads.trigger: If your defender fights over the screen or there's no help, attack the rim. If you feel a body on your back or the lane clogs, plant and short roll

reads.situation: You're setting the back screen for 4
progression: First look: Set a solid screen and hold it
Second look: Slip to the rim if your defender shows early or switches onto 4
Third look: Roll to the left block after 4 clears for offensive rebound position
reads.trigger: If 4's defender goes under and your man hedges or shows, slip immediately before contact. Otherwise, screen and dive

1.job: You start the play with the entry pass to 5, relocate to the right wing to receive the swing pass, then make the read on whether to hit 2 on the wing, 4 on the dive, or 5 on the slip
keys: After your initial pass, sprint to relocate on the right side—don't drift, get there with purpose so 4 can hit you in rhythm
When you catch on the wing, be a threat to shoot so your defender has to respect you
Eyes on your defender first—his reaction tells you whether 2 is open
1.commonError: Relocating too slowly after the entry pass, which delays the swing and lets the defense recover

2.job: You make a basket cut in the first beat to occupy help, then cut through in the second beat to clear out, then fill to the right wing in the third beat as the primary kick-out option
keys: Your cut through in beat 2 has to take your defender with you—don't float, sell it like you want the ball
Time your fill to the wing so you arrive as 4 is coming off the screen—too early and you clog, too late and the window closes
Catch ready to shoot—this only works if the defense thinks you'll pull it
2.commonError: Drifting to the wing too early or too high, which shrinks the spacing and lets one defender guard both you and 4

3.job: You stay in the corner on the left side to occupy your defender and prevent help-side rotation—you likely won't touch the ball, but you keep the weak side honest
keys: Stay below the break in the corner until the ball gets to the right side
If your defender sinks into the lane to help on 4's cut, call for it—you might get a skip pass for a corner three
Don't drift up or in—the moment you leave the corner, your defender becomes a help defender
3.commonError: Creeping toward the action or above the break, which allows your defender to help on 4's dive without consequence

4.job: You cut in the first beat to reposition, then serve as the hub in the swing from 5 to 1, then use 5's back screen to cut hard to the rim for the primary finish
keys: On the swing, catch and move it immediately to 1—you're not looking to score here, you're moving the defense
Set up the back screen by giving 5 a target—step toward the ball before you cut so the screen creates separation
Cut off the screen with your hands ready—if 1's defender helps, the pass is coming
4.commonError: Holding the ball too long on the catch from 5, which lets the defense recover and eliminates the advantage of the quick swing

5.job: You receive the entry pass from 1, initiate the swing to 4, then set a back screen for 4 and dive to the rim or slip if the defense shows
keys: Catch the entry and immediately look to reverse it—we're not hunting your shot here, we're moving the ball
On the back screen, get your butt into 4's defender's thigh and hold it—don't just brush by
After you screen, read your defender—if he helps hard, slip before he recovers; if he stays home, roll to the weak side for the board
5.commonError: Setting the screen too high or at a bad angle, which lets 4's defender slide under and stay attached

spacingRules: 3 stays in the left corner until the ball swings to the right side—if you drift up, your defender helps and the play dies
1 must relocate to the right wing with urgency after the entry pass—passive relocation kills the timing of the swing
2 clears all the way through on the second beat before filling to the wing—if you hang in the lane, there's no room for 4 to cut
4 sets up the back screen by creating space first—if you're standing on top of 5 when he goes to screen, there's no separation

counters.trigger: 4's defender fights over the top of the back screen and stays attached
counters.response: 5 slips to the rim immediately before setting the screen, and 1 hits him on the slip
counters.why: If the defender is overplaying the screen, his momentum takes him away from the slip, and 5's man can't recover in time to help

counters.trigger: The defense switches the back screen
counters.response: 4 short rolls to the elbow or mid-post area, and 5 seals the smaller defender on the block
counters.why: The switch creates a mismatch—either 4 has a size advantage in the middle or 5 has one on the block, and we take whichever is more open

counters.trigger: 1's defender sinks in to help on 4's cut
counters.response: 1 immediately hits 2 on the wing for the catch-and-shoot three
counters.why: If 1's defender commits to the help, he can't recover to contest 2 in time, and that's the shot we want as the counter

counters.trigger: 3's defender leaves the corner to help on the back screen
counters.response: 1 skips it to 3 in the corner for the wide-open three
counters.why: We've forced help from two passes away, which means the defense is scrambling—3 will be alone, and the skip pass beats the rotation

situations: After a timeout when you need a high-percentage look
Against man-to-man defense that struggles with back screens
When 4 has a speed or athleticism advantage over his defender
When 2 is a good shooter and the defense respects it
Early in the shot clock to get an easy basket before the defense sets
commonBreakdowns: 1 relocates slowly after the entry pass, so the swing from 4 to 1 is late and the defense recovers before the back screen
2 fills to the wing too early, clogging the driving lane for 4 and making the defense's help easier
5 sets a lazy or high back screen that 4's defender can easily get under
4 doesn't sell the cut hard enough, so his defender doesn't commit and can stay in position to contest
3 drifts out of the corner, allowing his defender to become a free help defender on 4's dive without consequence
1 doesn't read his own defender first—he looks for 4 even when the kick to 2 is wide open
The swing from 5 to 4 to 1 is too slow, giving the defense time to shift and eliminating the rotational advantage

Is there a specific game situation when you call this—ATO, need-a-bucket, against a particular opponent?

Idaho.intent: 5 coming off a cross-screen from 3 at the elbow for a post catch or seal on the weak side
Idaho.advantage: The cross-screen from 3 creates separation for 5 to establish position, while 1's dribble to the wing and the pass to 4 shifts the defense away from the help side where 5 is cutting
Idaho.entry: 1 dribbles up to initiate while 3, 4, and 5 all relocate—3 moves to the elbow area, 4 drops to the corner/wing, and 5 starts from the weak-side block

beatPurposes.b1: Set up the alignment—get 3 to the screening position at the elbow, 4 to the ball-side wing to receive, and 5 to the weak-side block to use the screen
beatPurposes.b2: Execute the primary action—3 screens for 5 cutting across while 1 passes to 4 to create the feeding angle

reads.situation: You catch on the wing as 5 is coming off 3's screen
progression: First look is 5 sealing after the screen—hit it if defender trails or gets caught on the screen
Second look is 5 posting up if the defender goes under but 5 establishes position
Safety is reverse it back to 1 or swing to 2 if nothing's there
reads.trigger: Where 5's defender is relative to the screen—trailing means seal and feed, fronting means look for the lob or reset

reads.situation: You're dribbling toward the wing to make the pass to 4
progression: First look is can you feed 5 directly if the angle opens
Primary action is hit 4 on the wing to let them make the entry
Keep yourself available for the reversal if 4 can't get it in
reads.trigger: If 5's defender loses position early and you have the angle, skip 4 and go direct—otherwise execute the pass to 4

1.job: You're the initiator. Dribble up and to the wing to create the passing angle, then get the ball to 4 so they can feed 5. Be available for the reversal if it doesn't go in.
keys: Your dribble movement pulls the defense and creates the angle for 4 to feed
Don't rush the pass to 4—let 5's cut develop off the screen
Stay active after the pass—you're the safety valve
1.commonError: Passing to 4 too early before 5 is using the screen, killing the timing of the cut

2.job: You're the weak-side spacing. Hold the corner to keep your defender from helping on 5's cut. Be ready for a skip pass if the ball reverses.
keys: Stay in the corner—if you drift up, your defender can tag 5
Keep your hands ready—the skip can come fast if 4 gets stuck
2.commonError: Drifting toward the action to get involved, which brings a help defender into the paint

3.job: You're the screener. Set a solid cross-screen at the elbow for 5, then read what happens after—slip to the rim if your defender helps hard, or pop if the lane clogs.
keys: Screen angle matters—set it so 5 can cut to the block or seal in the lane
Make contact and hold it—this isn't a brush screen
After the screen, read your defender—if they help on 5, slip; if they stay, relocate to keep spacing
3.commonError: Setting the screen too high or too soft, so 5 doesn't get clean separation from their defender

4.job: You're the feeder. Catch on the wing from 1, then look to feed 5 coming off 3's screen. Read where 5's defender is and make the right entry pass.
keys: Catch ready to pass—the window to feed 5 is short
Read the seal—if 5's defender trails, hit the pocket immediately
If you can't feed, reverse it quickly—don't hold it and let the defense recover
4.commonError: Holding the ball too long looking for a perfect entry instead of hitting 5 when they're open or reversing it

5.job: You're the primary scorer. Use 3's screen to get position on the weak side, then seal your defender and call for the ball from 4. Finish strong when it comes.
keys: Set your defender up—take them low or wide before using the screen
Come off the screen hard and establish position immediately—this is about leverage, not speed
Seal with your body and show your hands as a target for 4
5.commonError: Floating off the screen instead of making contact and sealing, letting your defender recover position

spacingRules: 2 stays in the corner until the ball moves—your defender cannot be allowed to tag 5's cut
3 sets the screen at the elbow, not above it—too high and 5 can't get to the block
4 must be in position on the wing before 1 passes—if you're not there, the feeding angle doesn't exist
1 clears to the top after passing to maintain reversal option and keep the strong-side guard from digging down

counters.trigger: 5's defender fights over the top of 3's screen
counters.response: 3 slips to the rim immediately while 5 pops short—4 reads which one is open
counters.why: If the defender is chasing over, they can't stop 3 from diving and 5 has space for the short feed

counters.trigger: 5's defender goes under the screen and fronts the post
counters.response: 5 seals for the lob or 1 reverses to 2 for the skip and a different attack
counters.why: Fronting takes away the direct feed but gives up the lob if 4 can make that pass, or we reset with better spacing

counters.trigger: 2's defender leaves the corner to tag 5's cut
counters.response: 4 skips it immediately to 2 in the corner for the open three
counters.why: That's what 2 is there for—if the help comes from the corner, the corner is open

counters.trigger: 3's defender shows hard or switches onto 5
counters.response: 3 slips to the rim while 5 pops or flares—both can't be covered
counters.why: If 3's defender commits to 5, 3 has the advantage going to the basket; if they switch, there's a mismatch somewhere

situations: Against teams that don't help aggressively—if they stay home, 5 gets clean post touches
When you need a high-percentage look and want to get your post player involved
After a timeout when you can walk through the alignment and timing
commonBreakdowns: 1 passes to 4 before 5 is even using the screen—kills the whole timing and 5's defender recovers easily
3 sets a lazy screen or sets it too high, so 5 never gets the separation needed to seal
2 drifts up from the corner to watch, bringing a help defender into the lane right where 5 is trying to post
5 doesn't set up the screen—just jogs into it without creating any separation first, making it easy to defend

Kansas.intent: 3 coming off a down screen from 5 at the elbow for a catch-and-shoot on the wing, with 2 at the top as the reversal option
Kansas.advantage: The screen from 5 at the elbow creates separation for 3 cutting from the corner to the wing. Simultaneous action — 2's initial basket cut and 4's corner fill — occupies help defenders so 3's defender can't get early help over the screen.
Kansas.entry: 1 starts at the top with the ball. 2 is on the right wing, 5 at the left elbow, 3 in the left corner, 4 in the right corner. Entry pass goes to 2, who immediately basket cuts to clear out, then ball reverses through 1 to 5 at the elbow.

beatPurposes.b1: 2's basket cut clears the right side and occupies help defense. Gets their defender away from the action and sets up the reversal.
beatPurposes.b2: Ball gets to 5 at the elbow. This is the trigger position — 5 needs the ball to make the down screen work and create the passing angle to 3 on the wing.
beatPurposes.b3: The money beat. 5 screens for 3 cutting to the wing for the shot. 2 relocates to the top as the pressure release. 4 fills the right corner to maintain spacing and provide a second-side option.

reads.situation: You have the ball at the elbow and you're about to set the down screen for 3
progression: First look is 3 coming off your screen to the wing — hit them for the catch-and-shoot if their defender trails or goes under
Second look is 2 at the top if 3's defender fights over and denies the wing pass
If 3's defender shows hard on the screen, slip to the basket before you complete the screen
reads.trigger: How 3's defender plays the screen tells you everything. Trailing or under means hit 3. Fighting over top means skip to 2. Showing hard on you means slip.

reads.situation: You're cutting off 5's screen from the corner to the wing
progression: Primary is catch-and-shoot on the wing if you're open
If your defender chases over the top and 5 slips, look to feed 5 on the roll
If the pass doesn't come, continue through and relocate — don't stand and watch
reads.trigger: Hands ready as you come off the screen. If the ball goes to 2 at the top instead, you become the second-side option.

reads.situation: You've basket cut and relocated to the top
progression: If you receive from 5, look to swing to 3 on the wing immediately if their defender is trailing
Attack the closeout if the defense has rotated and you catch with an advantage
Reversal to 4 in the opposite corner if the defense collapses to 3's side
reads.trigger: When 5 passes to you instead of 3, it's because 3 is denied. The defense is overplaying strong side — the answer is usually on the second side with 4.

1.job: You're the initiator. Make the entry pass to 2, get the ball back, then hit 5 at the elbow. After that, space to the weak side and be ready for a skip pass if the ball swings back out.
keys: Crisp passes — don't float it to 5, the timing matters
After you pass to 5, relocate to balance the floor, usually opposite wing
Stay above the break so you're a release valve
1.commonError: Drifting too far toward the corner after passing to 5, which shrinks the floor and makes you unavailable as an outlet

2.job: You're the space creator and the safety valve. Make a hard basket cut on the catch to clear out, then relocate to the top. You're the release if 3 is denied.
keys: Your basket cut has to be a real threat — sell it, occupy the help
Sprint to the top after your cut, don't jog — timing matters for 5's passing window
Catch ready to shoot at the top, defense will be scrambling if the ball comes to you
2.commonError: Lazy basket cut that doesn't actually pull your defender, leaving them in position to help on 3

3.job: You're the primary scorer. Set up your defender in the corner, then explode off 5's screen to the wing for the catch-and-shoot. Use the screen — don't drift away from it.
keys: Wait for 5 to get set — if you go too early, there's no screen
Cut shoulder-to-shoulder off the screen, tight enough that your defender has to go around
Hands up and ready as you come off — this is a catch-and-shoot, not a catch-and-think
3.commonError: Fading toward the sideline instead of cutting tight off the screen, which gives your defender an easy path to recover

4.job: You're the second-side spacing. Hold the right corner until the action happens, then cut to fill the opposite corner when 5 screens. Keep the defense honest — they can't help off you.
keys: Don't move too early — wait until 5 has the ball at the elbow
Fill to the corner, not the wing — we need corner spacing for drive-and-kick if the ball swings back
Be ready to catch and shoot, you're live if the defense collapses strong side
4.commonError: Drifting up toward the wing instead of staying in the corner, which kills the spacing and eliminates the skip pass angle

5.job: You're the hub. Catch at the elbow, read 3's defender, then either hit 3 on the wing or kick to 2 at the top. Your screen creates the shot, and your decision gets the ball to the right place.
keys: Set the screen at the elbow level, not too high — 3 needs room to get to the wing
Screen and immediate look to pass — you're not rolling hard here, you're facilitating
If their defender shows on you, slip before the screen is set
5.commonError: Setting the screen too high toward the free throw line, which forces 3 out to the three-point line with no room to operate

spacingRules: Corner players (3 and 4) stay in the corners until the ball is at the elbow with 5 — early movement kills the spacing
2 must relocate all the way to the top of the key, not halfway — you need to pull your defender out and create the passing lane to 3
After the initial reversal, 1 must get above the break on the weak side — if you sink too low, you're not a viable outlet and the defense can load up strong side
When 4 fills to the opposite corner, stay wide — don't creep toward the lane

counters.trigger: 3's defender fights over the top of the screen and denies the wing pass
counters.response: 5 skips to 2 at the top, then 2 reverses to 4 on the second side or attacks the scrambling defense
counters.why: If they're denying 3 that hard, they're overcommitted strong side. The weak side is open and the defense is rotating late.

counters.trigger: 3's defender shows hard on 5 before the screen is set, trying to blow up the action
counters.response: 5 slips to the basket immediately instead of completing the screen, 3 looks to feed 5 on the roll
counters.why: When the defender commits to the screener, the screener becomes the open man. Don't run into a trap — take the advantage they're giving you.

counters.trigger: Help defender from the weak side tags 3 coming off the screen
counters.response: 3 skip passes to 4 in the corner on the second side, or 2 at the top reverses it quickly
counters.why: If weak-side help is tagging, someone is open on the backside. The ball has to get there before the defense rotates back.

counters.trigger: Defender goes under the screen on 3
counters.response: 3 stops at the elbow for the mid-range jumper or 5 hits 3 immediately and 3 attacks the closeout downhill
counters.why: Going under gives 3 space. If 3 can shoot the mid-range, take it. If not, the defender has to recover and 3 can attack the scrambling closeout.

Against man-to-man defense that doesn't switch — this falls apart against a switching team
After a timeout when you need an organized set to get a good shot
When 3 has a size or speed advantage over their defender and can use the screen effectively
Late shot clock reset — this is a quick-hitter that can get a shot in 6-8 seconds if executed sharply

5 sets the screen too high, forcing 3 out to the three-point line with no driving room
4 drifts up from the corner toward the wing, shrinking the floor and eliminating the second-side skip pass

Kentucky.intent: 4 coming off a down screen from 3 for a catch-and-shoot jumper at the top of the key or elbow area
Kentucky.advantage: The initial motion scrambles the defense with multiple cuts, then we use 3's down screen to free up 4 while the defense is still recovering. 5 at the nail occupies the middle help defender.
Kentucky.entry: 1 passes to 2 on the wing and immediately relocates. This triggers the motion—everyone moves off the pass.

beatPurposes.b1: Scramble the defense with cuts and get the ball to the wing. 3 cutting down gets their defender moving ballside, setting up the screen. 4 cutting to the top looks like they're clearing but really they're getting position to come back off the screen.
beatPurposes.b2: This is the money beat. 4 uses 3's down screen to get separation for the shot. 2 hits 5 at the nail as a connector—5 has the angle to hit 4 coming off. The dribble from 2 shifts the defense and creates the passing angle.
beatPurposes.b3: Continuation if 4 doesn't shoot. 5 can hit cutters or we reset into secondary action. This beat keeps the defense moving if the primary shot isn't there.

reads.situation: You catch the pass on the wing
progression: First look: if your defender trails you on the cut, turn the corner to the rim
Second: hit 5 at the nail to reverse it
Safety: dribble to create the angle for the pass to 5
reads.trigger: If the defense is scrambling to find 3 and 4, attack. If they recover, hit 5 and let the screen work.

reads.situation: You receive at the nail from 2
progression: First look: 4 coming off 3's screen—hit them the moment they show hands
Second: if 4's defender fights over hard, 3 should be open slipping to the basket
Safety: swing to 1 on the opposite wing and we run secondary
reads.trigger: Read 4's defender. If they trail or go under, hit 4 immediately. If they fight over and bump 3, look at 3 slipping.

reads.situation: You're coming off 3's down screen
progression: First look: catch and shoot if you're open
Second: if your defender goes under, take the dribble pull-up
